newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden lifts sawn timber exports to Japan - industry.
newsitem.headline: Sweden lifts sawn timber exports to Japan - industry.

text.p: Swedish exports of sawn wood to Japan doubled in 1996 to almost 400,000 cubic metres and are expected to continue growing strongly this year, Sweden's forestry products export association said on Thursday.

"We expect deliveries to reach almost 400,000 cubic metres last year ... and it can be 600,000-700,000 cubic metres this year," the group's chief analyst Lars-Goran Olsson told a forestry seminar in Stockholm.
Olsson forecast a strong wood products market with rising prices.
"We can see a market that is characterised by a surplus in demand," Olsson said.
The biggest wood product importers in Western Europe imported 25.5 million cubic metres in 1996, according to the association's estimates.
The forecast for 1997 is a little higher at 26.2 million cubic metres. But Swedish exports to these countries are seen falling.

"We think our deliveries to Europe will decrease this year. This does depend partly on continuing to increase volumes to Japan but also on increased consumption in Sweden combined with lower Swedish stocks," Olsson said.
He said there was some need to increase production to meet demand.
The total Swedish production of sawn wood in 1996 was about 14.4 million cubic metres.
